assumptions: The reminder addresses LCs generally for impact assessment; appropriate operational changes depend on their business impact.
The exact attachment of 'where appropriate' remains unresolved.
The qualitative adequacy and preparation timing requirements are retained without inventing numerical thresholds.

citations.quote: the SFC wishes to remind licensed corporations (LCs) to assess the impact of the Transition on their businesses and take appropriate measures to maintain their smooth and effective operations after the Transition.
These include enhancing their operational processes, technological infrastructure and systems as well as staffing arrangements where appropriate.
Proactively engaging and communicating with their clients who are potentially affected by the Transition in order to raise their awareness and facilitate their preparations for a smooth transition.

Effective 28 May 2024, the standard settlement cycle for transactions in US securities1 will be shortened from two business days after the trade date (T+2) to one business day after trading (T+1) (the Transition)2.
1 Such as equities, bonds, exchange-traded funds and options.
The reference to the Transition in this circular includes the transition in the US and Canada.

node.5f3372e2b3e81119ac80281f.distinction: Assessment is addressed generally to LCs, while changes depend on appropriateness and communication targets potentially affected clients. A narrow grammatical attachment makes only staffing enhancements expressly conditional; a broader attachment makes all listed enhancements expressly conditional. Neither reading supplies a blanket exemption from assessing impact or being ready.
questions: Does 'where appropriate' attach solely to staffing arrangements or to the whole enhancement list?
How early must communication occur to facilitate client preparations?
Which specific securities transactions fall within the standard-cycle change? The illustrative product list does not resolve every transaction.
node.5f3372e2b3e81119ac80281f.statement: [TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT] The selected LC assessment and preparation control is satisfied when the LC assesses the US and Canadian Transition's business impact, takes appropriate measures to maintain smooth and effective operations afterward, and proactively engages potentially affected clients to support awareness and preparation. Securities examples are non-exhaustive. The effective dates describe market transitions, not a newly invented start date for preparation duties.
node.5f3372e2b3e81119ac80281f.subject: LC impact assessment, proportionate enhancements and client preparation

assumptions: The selected control is an LC operational-readiness outcome, not a certification that every listed method was used.
Client engagement is assessed only where clients are potentially affected.

citations.quote: LCs should assess their readiness and ensure they are able to cope with the shortened settlement cycle, including:
Ensuring the availability of staff to complete the post-trade settlement processes within the shortened timeframe.
Proactively engaging and communicating with their clients who are potentially affected by the Transition in order to raise their awareness and facilitate their preparations for a smooth transition.

LCs may consider adjusting their staff’s work shifts, extending working hours or arranging evening or morning duties in conjunction with automating their operational processes to enable timely trade settlements.

node.98355b0411b875e6dc6570fe.distinction: Reading A treats “including” as introducing representative controls supporting the overarching outcome: the LC has assessed readiness and can cope with the shortened cycle. The optional scheduling and automation measures are methods, not mandatory elements. Liquidity, staffing and training evidence informs whether the outcome is achieved, while client engagement applies when clients are potentially affected.

node.ad90b99e5f5f57d54f7b0f43.distinction: Reading A treats the LC language as a supervisory readiness outcome: the LC must assess and be able to cope, while the listed staffing methods are examples selected according to circumstances. Reading B treats each listed 'should' item as a separate expected control, so readiness is compliant only when liquidity/funding, staffing/training, and client communication controls are each established; the source does not expressly resolve whether every item is mandatory.

node.cf9271c3592435923d164bee.distinction: Reading B treats the readiness outcome and each enumerated “should” item as cumulative controls: failure of any applicable liquidity/funding, staff availability, training, or client-engagement control means the selected control is not compliant. “Where appropriate,” “potentially affected,” and the cross-currency qualifier limit applicability, while the may sentence preserves discretion over particular staffing methods.
